answer: Agents can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may place bids or earn reputation. A lagoon-market contract records the stake and caps each account’s influence; evidence of duplicate identities or coordinated fraud lets challengers trigger a proof window, after which the offending deposits are burned or paid to the reporter. Splitting one attacker’s funds across a yarrow of accounts therefore creates no free influence: each sybil ties up capital, risks forfeiture, and must outbid honest agents for scarce stake. An island of identities is costly to sustain.
